name: Uzbek, Northern
confidence_why: Sjoberg 1963 calls Uzbek stress phonemic but places it on the final syllable by default, and Athanasopoulou, Vogel & Dolatian 2020 read the same facts as Turkish-type final stress with pre-stressing suffixes and lexical exceptions and find acoustic support for final prominence, so excluding Uzbek as a lexical-stress language is the weaker reading.
catalog_citation: Kononov, A. N. 1960. Grammatika sovremennogo uzbekskogo literaturnogo jazyka. Moskva–Leningrad: Izdatel'stvo Akademii Nauk SSSR. 446 pp.
catalog_locator: pp. 52-55, §§50-53 'Slovesnoe udarenie' (word stress; phrasal stress is §57, p. 56)
catalog_quote: Все слова узбекского языка в отношении акцентуации могут быть разбиты на две группы: 1) слова с силовым ударением на последнем слоге; 2) слова с силовым ударением не на последнем слоге. § 51. Силовое ударение на последнем слоге наблюдается, как правило, в двусложных именах существительных, прилагательных, глаголах … [p. 53] В многосложных словах силовое ударение, как правило, падает на последний слог … [p. 54] § 53. Силовое ударение не на последнем слоге имеет место в следующих случаях: 1. Во всех лицах повелительного наклонения, в 1-м л. ед. и мн. ч. желательного наклонения и в именах числительных количественных ударение строго обязательно, а в наречиях, местоимениях и междометиях, как правило, падает на первый слог … [p. 55] 2. Во всех случаях, когда к основе присоединяется безударный аффикс (энклитика): студéнтман ‘я студент’

tone_statements.citation: Jamolxonov, Hasanboy. 2009. O'zbek tilining nazariy fonetikasi ('O'zbek tili'dan o'quv qo'llanma). Toshkent: Fan.
tone_statements.quote: Ўзбек тилида ҳам мусиқий урғу йўқ, аммо унда чўзиқлик белгиси ва зарб бор. Бу белгилар урғули бўғинни шу сўздаги урғусиз бўғинлардан ажратиш имконини беради. ... Демак, ўзбек тилидаги сўз урғусида зарб биринчи ўринда туради, шунга кўра уни динамик урғу деб баҳолаш мақсадга мувофиқдир. Мусиқий (тоник, мелодик) урғу япон, хитой, корейс тилларига хосдир.
tone_statements.translation: Uzbek too has no musical stress, but it does have the length feature and force (intensity). These features make it possible to distinguish the stressed syllable from the unstressed syllables of the word. ... Thus in Uzbek word stress force comes first, so it is appropriate to assess it as dynamic stress. Musical (tonic, melodic) stress is characteristic of Japanese, Chinese and Korean.
tone_statements.locator: p.165, 32-§ Урғу (Акцентема), I.1 (фонетик табиатига кўра сўз урғуси)
tone_statements.summary: States Uzbek has no musical (tonic/melodic) accent: word stress is dynamic and final; pitch appears only in syntagma/phrase intonation.

sources.citation: Sjoberg 1963:23 §2.412, sjoberg1963/, read visually); Ido 2025 JIPA (our earlier reading)
sources.quote: § 50. Словесное ударение в узбекском языке силовое, или динамическое … [p. 56] § 57. Фразовое ударение, назначение которого — сообщать данному предложению определенный оттенок, в фонетическом отношении совершенно независимо и не связано ни с какими чисто фонетическими нормами.

sources.citation: Athanasopoulou, Angeliki, Irene Vogel & Hossep Dolatian. 2020. Acoustic properties of word and phrasal prominence in Uzbek. Proceedings of the Workshop on Turkic and Languages in Contact with Turkic 5: 1-15. doi:10.3765/ptu.v5i1.4796 (CC BY 4.0; LSA host could not be reached by automated download, archived copy (Internet Archive, 1 May 2024))
sources.quote: p.2: 'Like Turkish, Uzbek is reported to have final lexical stress ... Also like Turkish, Uzbek is reported to have, in addition to its canonical final stress, cases in which stress appears in other positions within a word. Specifically, we find a number of lexical exceptions, including loanwords, function words, and proper names ... In addition, there are certain affixes that may require stress to be placed prior to the final syllable' (pre-stressing -ma NEG, equatives, copular person particles; fn.2: 'there are some reports of secondary stress (Sjoberg 1963:31, Bodrogligeti 2003:37)'). p.12
sources.locator: p.2 §2 (descriptive summary, exx. from Sjoberg 1963:24-5); pp.11-12 §5.3 and §6 Conclusions
sources.note: First systematic acoustic study (8 Tashkent speakers, 3 focus conditions): final syllable longer with a falling contour in all conditions, read by the authors as supporting canonical final lexical stress; directly answers the 'Branch C phrasal-only' worry banked in the compilers note and contradicts keeping standard Uzbek out while every sister Turkic row is coded final.
sources.venue: Proceedings of the Workshop on Turkic and Languages in Contact with Turkic

sources.citation: Andronov, Aleksej V. & Nikita V. Suprunčuk (eds.). 2021. Iz akcentologičeskogo nasledija E. D. Polivanova ('K obščefonetičeskomu voprosu o funkcijax udarenija', 1931) [From Evgenij Polivanov's accentological heritage: 'The functions of accent as a problem of general phonetics' (1931)]. Indoevropejskoe jazykoznanie i klassičeskaja filologija 25(2): 1365-1406. St. Petersburg: ILI RAN. doi:10.30842/ielc230690152582.
sources.note: Read online: Uzbek figures only as a (final) word-stress language - Polivanov states Turkic stress is on the last syllable with 'deplacement' to the first syllable in finite verbs (Kazakh/Uzbek ketti) and in Uzbek vocatives (oj- + name), and parses a Tashkent-Uzbek sentence by its four word stresses to argue the delimitative function of Wortakzent; pitch enters only in his remark on Altaic 'two-pole' accent (force on the first syllable, pitch maximum on the last) as a possible Common-Altaic relic. No claim of lexical tone in Uzbek.

tone.quote: В турецких языках ударение (по крайней мере в большинстве турецких языков) на последнем слоге; но тем не менее в не которых случаях (напр., в verbum finitum или в вока-тивных предложениях) встречается и депласация ударения — на первый слог; напр., в казакском или узбекском глаголе (Praeteritum 3-го л.) ketti вместо ketti 'ушёл' (или — беру наиболее типичную форму узбекского вокативного предложения: префикс oj-, £j, -ej и т. д. + имя лица: esoqqul oj-esoyqul (слог oj получает сильнейшее уда-рение))
tone.locator: Polivanov's MS pp.25-26 as edited, in the passage on the 'two-pole' (dvuxpoljusnost') accent of the Altaic languages; printed article pp.1365-1406 (exact page not visible in the cyberleninka HTML); the Tashkent-dialect sentence parsed by its four word stresses follows at MS p.32.
tone.translation: In the Turkic languages the stress (at least in most Turkic languages) is on the last syllable; nevertheless in some cases (e.g. in the finite verb or in vocative sentences) a displacement of the stress onto the first syllable also occurs; e.g. in the Kazakh or Uzbek verb (3rd person preterite) kétti instead of kettí 'went away' (or, taking the most typical form of the Uzbek vocative sentence: prefix oj-, ej etc. + personal name: esoqqul oj-esoyqul (the syllable oj receives the strongest stress)).
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.summary: Uzbek treated as final dynamic stress with morphosyntactic stress shift; no lexical tone.

tone.quote: It can be observed in Figure 9 that the vowel duration increases in the final syllable and that both the mean frequency and mean intensity are the highest on the penultimate syllable. Given that previous descriptions of Uzbek are unanimous in locating the primary lexical stress on the final syllable (Kononov, 1960; Sjoborg, 1962; Bodrogligeti, 2003), one potentially feasible interpretation of these observations is that vowel duration correlates with lexical stress in native Uzbek words and/or that certain acoustic properties (such as a high f0) of the penultimate syllable contribute to the perceived prominence of the final syllable. ... the penultimate rise in f0 might also result from intonational phenomena such as pitch accents.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.summary: No lexical tone (prosody = final word stress; f0 treated as stress/intonation correlate).
